newsitem.title: CANADA: Westcoast to get nearly C$10 mln after deal.
newsitem.headline: Westcoast to get nearly C$10 mln after deal.

text.p: Westcoast Energy Inc said on Monday it would receive up to nearly C$10 million from PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd as a result of the suspension of the proposed Palliser Pipeline project.

Vancouver-based Westcoast, a 50-50 partner with PanCanadian in Palliser, which was essentially killed after a toll deal was reached between PanCanadian and NOVA Corp, said it would receive C$2.5 million to recover its costs together with a further C$1 million payment in 1996.
Under the original agreement, PanCanadian was obligated to reimburse Westcoast for project costs, it said.
Westcoast also said it would receive from PanCanadian a share of savings generated by the difference between NOVA's current toll and the proposed load retention rate, which was announced on Monday.
It was anticipated that in 1997, the payment would be C$5 million-C$6 million on a net present value basis, Westcoast said.
Westcoast spokeswoman Patricia Bowles said the funds that would be paid to the company had yet to be earmarked for a specific alternative purpose.
